claim: The 1966 MERCURY bulletin has formal Bell Telephone Laboratories memorandum metadata, including a numbered memorandum requirement.
scope: One 1966 MERCURY operational bulletin; document metadata only.

assessment.basis: Direct document text and form requirements.
limitations: does not establish a universal Bell Labs memorandum practice

claim: MERCURY supported author-selected and reader-requested routing of Technical Memoranda by recipient, organization, subject, author, author organization, and filing case.
scope: MERCURY workflow described in the 1966 bulletin.

sources.locator: PDF p. 1; Appendix A; Appendix B, PDF pp. 10-11

assessment.basis: The bulletin explicitly describes the distribution and request fields.

claim: The MERCURY workflow allowed author-directed delivery irrespective of reader request and left nonemployee responsibility to the author.
scope: MERCURY workflow described in the 1966 bulletin.

assessment.basis: Direct workflow exception in the bulletin.
limitations: historical policy is not a current authority model

relations.basis: It rules out copying MERCURY as a consent-preserving broker template.

claim: The supplied memorandum evidence does not support universal facts/model/speculation formatting, legal priority, an official three-loop model, or a universal BSTJ theory-to-implementation sequence.
scope: The supplied 1966 MERCURY bulletin and bounded corpus.

assessment.basis: No supplied source supports these asserted historical rules.
limitations: unsupported is not evidence that their negations are true

claim: Kelly's Bell System organization is described as a bridge from research through engineering, development, and manufacture, with systems engineering connecting backgrounds and operating contact.
scope: Pierce's biographical account of Kelly's organization.

assessment.basis: The memoir directly attributes the organizational description to Kelly and Pierce.

claim: The corpus does not establish intentional long-corridor causality for innovation; the claimed intention is attributed second-hand and the cited interaction evidence is mixed and confounded.
scope: Bell Labs corridor narrative and workplace-interaction discussion in the supplied source.

assessment.basis: The source describes corridors but treats intention as attributed and cautions against causal folklore.

relations.basis: Synthetic corridors or random-chat mechanisms have no licensed causal basis here.

claim: Weak interunit ties can aid search for useful nonredundant knowledge at lower maintenance cost, but can impede transfer of noncodified system-dependent knowledge; net completion-time effects depend on complexity.
scope: 120 projects in 41 divisions of one electronics company; primary transfer analysis N=54; completion time outcome.

sources.locator: printed pp. 83-88, Table 2 and Figure 2, pp. 99-105

assessment.basis: The paper reports the search/transfer distinction and complexity interaction.
limitations: completion time is not scientific value

relations.basis: It supports separating attention/reach from local evaluation and transfer.

claim: Team expertise coordination includes knowing where expertise is, where it is needed, and bringing it to bear; the reported performance association exceeds staffing and administrative coordination controls.
scope: 69 software development teams in the official abstract.

assessment.basis: The official abstract states the construct and association.

claim: Shared drawings can coordinate occupational work and carry feedback while omitting situated workmanship that concrete artifacts make available.
scope: One-firm ethnography of engineers, technicians, assemblers, drawings, and machines.

sources.locator: printed pp. 729-733, Table 1 p. 730, and pp. 744-746

assessment.basis: The study documents both coordination and omitted local practice.
limitations: does not prescribe a universal format

relations.basis: It motivates, but does not prove, testing concrete bounded context in offers.

claim: In two corporate office redesign studies, open workspaces reduced measured face-to-face interaction while electronic interaction increased; channel change did not measure collaboration quality or broker utility.

assessment.basis: The paper reports channel-specific interaction changes and its outcome boundary.
limitations: no consented offers or LLM agents

relations.basis: Visibility or broadcast cannot be assumed to create useful interaction.

claim: The repository assigns local state admission and commitment to Section Directors; the Programme Supervisor is cold, portfolio-only, and excluded from method prose and lateral-transfer interpretation.
scope: Current repository authority contract at HEAD 146d0ee63d0cb89b13e7225fa8896e97e8279174.

limitations: present-state contract, not external empirical evidence

relations.basis: The offer path must preserve local Director ownership and Supervisor blindness.

claim: Human method proposals are quarantined as non-authoritative HUMAN-METHOD-INPUT and are usable only after independent local admission; raw wording must not reach the Programme Supervisor.

assessment.basis: Explicit local input quarantine and schema.
limitations: existing schema lacks consent, expiry, withdrawal, offer digest, and recipient binding

relations.basis: A pulled offer can enter only as the existing non-authoritative input category.

claim: The committed-learning bus is receipt-grounded and commit-gated; pre-admission encounter offers must not reuse SECTION_TRANSFER_PACKET or transfer semantics, and propagation does not earn SEARCH or LEARN credit.
scope: Current cross-section learning and event validation contract at HEAD 146d0ee63d0cb89b13e7225fa8896e97e8279174.

assessment.basis: The architecture, packet schema, and validator require committed receipt lineage.
limitations: present-state contract, not a broker implementation

relations.basis: Offers must be a separate pre-admission path and cannot create scientific credit.

claim: Documentation governance can govern durable locus and lineage but cannot decide semantic admission or artifact meaning.

The authority-safe local design is consented encounter -> declassified non-authoritative expiring offer -> voluntary Section Director pull/record as HUMAN-METHOD-INPUT -> independent ADMIT|REJECT|DEFER; expiry, withdrawal, or no pull terminate without state mutation.
scope: A proposed manual/shadow broker overlay; not a runtime implementation or efficacy claim.

assessment.basis: Configurative design inference: external sources motivate bounded attention and local transfer limits; local contracts determine authority semantics.
limitations: must not copy historical MERCURY consent exceptions

relations.basis: The content requirement is a separate pilotable inference.

claim: An offer should contain a bounded concrete example or discriminator sufficient for a Director to decide whether to pull, while remaining non-authoritative.
scope: Proposed offer-content hypothesis for a manual/shadow pilot.

assessment.basis: Design inference from situated-artifact limits plus the existing local admission boundary.
limitations: content must remain declassified and bounded

claim: Receipt-linked scientific LEARN per wall-clock hour is the North Star; memos, offers, pulls, agents, tokens, fan-out, replay, and delivery are diagnostics or denominators only and never scientific credit.
scope: Frozen evaluation rule for the proposed pilot.

assessment.basis: The current architecture expressly excludes propagation metrics from SEARCH and LEARN credit; the named North Star is the frozen decision rule.
limitations: does not itself measure broker efficacy

claim: Whether consented, expiring encounter offers improve LLM-agent research outcomes without harming authority, attention, or throughput is unknown.
scope: Human-organization findings transferred to the proposed LLM-agent research harness.

assessment.basis: All external empirical evidence concerns human organizations; no supplied evidence evaluates this broker or LLM agents.

relations.basis: The design contract is not evidence of efficacy.

claim: A manual/shadow pilot can test whether exact opt-in, expiring offers produce voluntary Director pulls and independently admitted tests without Supervisor visibility, global broadcast, blocking, or credit inflation.
scope: Pilot feasibility and contract conformance, not causal innovation efficacy.

assessment.basis: This is a testable pilot hypothesis derived from the design boundary, not a demonstrated result.
limitations: must measure withdrawals, expiries, no-pulls, attention cost, and contract violations
